title: Compact icon toggle: progressive loading skeleton and graceful fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Replace several ad-hoc icon-only button behaviors with a single compact toggle pattern that shows a progressive loading skeleton when an action is awaiting server confirmation, supports a cancelable escape path, and degrades gracefully to a disabled state when the runtime signals rate-limit or fallback. This ticket focuses on the visual system (tokens, spacing, motion), interaction model, and handoff artifacts for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: New compact icon toggle component appears in Figma with token-driven variants: default, active, loading-skeleton, disabled, fallback
Loading skeleton animation uses single token 'button.loading.duration' and respects reduced-motion preference
Interaction shows a small inline cancel affordance after 500ms of pending state; clicking cancel reverts to previous state without eager network call
Accessibility: each state has an accessible label and role; loading state exposes 'aria-busy' and an accessible cancel button is keyboard-focusable
Visual parity tests (Chromatic) added for desktop and mobile scales; snapshots created for light/dark themes and high-contrast
Engineering has a clear token map and a migration guide for replacing legacy icon-only classes
Runtime fallback guidance documented: how to switch to a lower-cost icon variant and how to display 'offline' style when rate-limited
design_notes: Introduce token 'button.compact.gap' (4px) and 'button.compact.hitTarget' (36px) to normalize hit areas across icon-only variants
Loading skeleton: single circular shimmer using 'motion.skeleton.direction=left-to-right' and opacity ramp tokens; avoid layout shift by reserving space with 'skeleton.reserve=true' token
Cancel affordance: initially visually hidden; reveal at 500ms pending and expose as a 20px tap target with tactile focus ring. Use icon 'x-small-close' and label 'Cancel action' for screen readers
Fallback style: mild red/orange glow only when server returns explicit 'fallback' flag; otherwise use disabled tone. Map these colors to semantic tokens rather than literal hex values
The component should read theme token aliases (semantic tokens) to ensure consistent appearance across light/dark and brand overrides
Edge case: if the action triggers a navigation, we show a transient spinner only and skip cancel affordance to avoid complex rollback UX
decisions: Use token-first approach: all measurements, colors, motion durations come from design tokens; no component-level hardcoded values
Expose two signals to engineers: 'pendingType' (short | extended) and 'serverFallback' (boolean). 'short' maps to a 300ms shimmer; 'extended' shows cancel affordance at 500ms
Accessibility: prefer aria-live polite only on state changes; do not use assertive to avoid interrupting screen reader users
Do not change existing large button tokens—this is intentionally scoped to compact/icon-only variants to reduce regression risk

review_feedback: PM Priya: make cancel copy explicit — 'Cancel' instead of 'Undo' for clarity
Engineering James: prefer exposing 'onCancel' hook and leave retry semantics to the caller; avoid internal optimistic attempts
Accessibility Sofia: request explicit keyboard focus order for inline cancel; ensure hit target meets 44x44mm guideline on touch devices
Design Maya: prefer single animation curve across all skeletons (ease-out-quad) to simplify runtime implementation
qa_checks: Snapshot tests: light/dark/high-contrast for each variant
Keyboard navigation: Tab to icon toggle -> Enter toggles -> Tab shows cancel affordance -> Enter cancels
Screen reader: verify aria-busy, aria-pressed, and live-region announcements for each state
Reduced motion: animations disabled and transitions replaced with cross-fade
Throttle simulation: verify fallback style appears when server returns 429/rate-limit payload
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Design handoff (this ticket): tokens, figma components, and acceptance criteria delivered to eng
Phase 2 - Engineering integration: implement component behind feature flag; expose it in a subset of admin pages
Phase 3 - Canary: enable for 10% of traffic with telemetry events 'compactToggle.pending' and 'compactToggle.cancel'
Phase 4 - Full rollout: remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stability and zero regressions
Post-release: monitor Console 'interaction-error' and 'accessibility-issues' dashboards for regressions
